DI G BAGONG "UPWAS Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG-NAPOLCOM Center, EDSA cor. Quezon Avenue, West Triangle, Quezon City www.dilq.qov.ph s. 2624- nv-G NO. AUG 21 HON. MARK ANTHONY A. TOLEDO Acting Vice Mayor Office of the Vice Mayor Bldg. B, 3rd Floor, Plaza Libertad, Poblacion II Silang, Cavite Dear Hon. Toledo: This has reference to your letter dated 03 June 2024 requesting the Department's opinion on the following matters, to wit: I. Did Acting Vice Mayor Mark Anthony Toledo lack the requisite authority to act as the presiding officer during the session of the Sangguniang Bayan of Silang on May 02, 2024, considering that he was not elected in accordance with Section 49(b) of the Local Government Code?l And 2. If Acting Vice Mayor Mark Anthony Toledo lacks the requisite authority to preside during the special session, are the resolutions passed during that session rendered invalid?2 Allow us first to restate the pertinent provision of the Local Government Code. Section 49(b)3 provides and we quote: Sec. 49(b) In the event of the inability of the regular presiding officer to preside at a sanggunian session, the members present and constituting a quorum shall elect from among themselves a temporary presiding officer. xxx The municipal Vice Mayor is the regular presiding officer of the Sangguniang Bayan, whenever the regular presiding officer fails to preside at the sangguniang session, the members present, constituting a quorum shall elect from among themselves a temporary presiding officer. While it is true that you have been designated as Vice Mayor in an acting capacity in view of the suspension order against Mayor Alston Kevin Anarna, it does not carry the position of being a presiding officer. Although, Part V, item No. 1 of DILG Memorandum Circular No. 2019-21 provides for the exceptions wherein the designated Acting Vice Mayor is prohibited from making or participating in any decisions enumerated therein and being a Presiding Officer Letter dated 03 June 2024 signed by Acting Vice Mayor Mark Anthony A. Tolledo Letter dated 03 June 2024 signed by Acting Vice Mayor Mark Anthony A. Tolledo Local Government Code of 1991 "Matino, Mahusay, at Maaasahan" Tel. (02) 8876-3454

does not fall under the aforesaid exceptions, still the Presiding Officership position is not automatically given because there is no automatic succession to the position of presiding officer in the occasion where the regular presiding officer (Vice Mayor) is temporarily unable to discharge his/her function as presiding officer. The powers, functions and duties given to an Acting Vice Mayor is merely temporary in nature and it does not erase the fact that the duly elected Vice Mayor is still the regular presiding officer. In the case at hand, wherein the Vice Mayor while being the Acting Mayor, temporarily relinquishes his/her power as presiding officer. As regards to your second query, the Department reiterates the Memorandum Order No. 2010-02 dated September 17, 2010 which states "The Department shall not act on queries of the following kinds, to wit: 1. Those containing facts that are justiciable in nature, Justiciable issues are those that require adjudication by the courts of law as to who between the opposing parties have the better right over a given controversy; 2. Those presumptively valid acts, e.g., enacted ordinances, consummated acts that already enjoy the presumption of regularity on the part of the public officer concerned, and similar instances; 3. Those that are litis pendencia or pending litigation, except when the court itself, requests for the opinion, In the event that an opinion has been rendered by the Department and its field officers without knowledge or information that a case involving the issues raised in the query is pending in court, such opinion shall automatically be deemed ineffective; and, 4. Those that are cognizable by other agencies of the government. Ordinances and resolutions enjoy the presumption of validity. Hence, until invalidated by a court, an ordinance is presumed valid and should be implemented notwithstanding any legal defect imputed against it. This legal defect, however, can be used as a ground to go to court in questioning that validity of the ordinance.4 Still, for ease of reference, we enumerate the requisites for its validity, to wit: a. It must not contravene the Constitution or any statute; b. Must not be unfair or oppressive; c. Must not be partial or discriminatory; d. Must not prohibit but may regulate trade; e. Must be general and consistent with public policy; and, f. Must not be unreasonable. In view thereof, it follows that the ordinances/resolutions passed by the Sanggunian presided by its member who was not expressly authorized by the members present is valid. It is worth noting that those legislative acts/enactments were passed by a majority vote of those present and its validity is not affected by the authority of the presiding officer being merely implied as signified by the acquiescence given by the members present. DILG opinion NO. 109 s.2007 Page 2 of3

This view is, however, without prejudice to the authoritative decision of the courts of competent jurisdiction. Hope we have enlightened you on the matter. Very truly yours, T THORITY OF THE SECRETARY: JUAN CTOR R. LLAMAS secretary for External, Legal and Legislative Affairs ELLA'JVRULLLS-LRALLD/agbl Page 3 of 3
